A bar graph with a scale that counts by 5s shows these totals: soccer 10, basketball 20, swimming 25, tennis 30. What is the total number for all four categories?
A bar graph with a scale that counts by 5s shows these totals: dogs 40, cats 10, fish 45, birds 5. How many are in fish and dogs together?
Which statement about place value is true?
e: 10 hundreds = 1,000. Ten ones make a ten, ten tens make a hundred, and ten thousands make ten thousand.

q: In the number 83,479, which digit is in the thousands place?
e: From the right: 9 ones, 7 tens, 4 hundreds, 3 thousands, 8 ten thousands.

q: In the fraction 1/6, what does the denominator 6 tell you?
o: The whole is split into 6 equal parts.
The fraction is 6 times as big as 1.
e: The denominator names how many equal parts the whole is partitioned into.

q: Which fraction is a unit fraction?
e: A unit fraction has a numerator of 1: one part of a whole split into equal parts.

q: Fatima shades 1 part of a bar split into 4 equal parts. Ravi shades 1 part of an identical bar split into 8 equal parts. Whose shaded part is larger?
o: Fatima's, because fourths are larger than eighths.
e: The more equal parts a whole is split into, the smaller each part is.

q: Which statement explains why 2/4 and 1/2 are equivalent fractions?
o: They name the same point on a number line.
e: Equivalent fractions name the same point on the number line or the same amount of the same-size whole.

q: Jada ate 3/6 of a pizza. Marco ate 1/2 of an identical pizza. Which statement is true?
o: They ate the same amount of pizza.
Marco ate more, because 2 is less than 6.
It is impossible to compare the amounts.
Jada ate more, because 3 is greater than 1.
e: 3/6 and 1/2 name the same part of the same-size whole, so they are equivalent.

q: Which pair of fractions is equivalent?
e: Splitting each third into 2 equal parts makes 2/3 into 4/6.

q: Mia ran 3/4 of a mile. Jon ran 3/8 of a mile. Who ran farther?
e: The numerators are the same; fourths are larger parts than eighths, so 3/4 > 3/8.

q: Which is greater, 1/3 or 1/6?
e: Thirds are larger pieces than sixths, so 1/3 > 1/6.

q: Which rule can you use to tell if a whole number is even?
o: It can be split into two equal groups with none left over.
e: Even numbers divide by 2 with nothing left over (they end in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8).

q: What is true about the sum of two odd numbers, such as 7 + 9?
o: The sum is always a multiple of 5.
The sum can be even or odd.
e: Two odd numbers pair up their extra ones, leaving no leftover: the sum is even.

q: Which statement matches the expression 5 × 12?
e: 5 × 12 compares: 5 times as much as 12.

q: Which three-dimensional figure has 6 square faces?
e: A cube has 6 faces, and every face is a square.

q: Which figure has one flat circular face, one curved surface, and one vertex?
e: A cone has a circular base, a curved surface, and a point (vertex) at the top.

q: Which figure has two circular faces and no vertices?
e: A cylinder has two flat circular faces joined by a curved surface.

q: How many vertices does a rectangular prism have?
e: A rectangular prism has 8 corners (vertices), 12 edges, and 6 faces.

q: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
e: A triangular prism has 2 triangular faces and 3 rectangular faces.

q: How many edges does a cube have?
e: A cube has 12 edges, 8 vertices, and 6 faces.

q: Which figure does NOT belong with the others?
e: The cylinder has a curved surface. The other three have only flat faces.

q: Which shape is NOT a quadrilateral?
e: A quadrilateral has exactly 4 sides; a triangle has 3.

q: Which statement is true?
o: Every rectangle is also a square.
Every square is also a rectangle.
e: A square has 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle with all sides equal.

q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and 2 pairs of parallel sides, but it has no right angles. Which shape is it?
e: Rectangles and squares have right angles, and a trapezoid has only one pair of parallel sides.

q: Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
e: A trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides.

q: A square is cut into 2 triangles of equal area along a diagonal. Each triangle is what fraction of the square?
e: Two equal parts make 1 whole, so each is 1/2.

q: Two identical rectangles are each cut into 4 parts with equal areas, but in different ways. Which statement is true?
o: Each part is 1/2 of its rectangle.
The parts cut differently cannot be fourths.
Each part is 1/4 of its rectangle, even if the parts look different.
e: Equal areas make equal shares: each of 4 equal-area parts is 1/4 of the whole.

q: Which situation is best for measuring liquid volume?
o: Finding how much water a pitcher holds
Finding how long a pitcher is
Finding how heavy a pitcher is when it is empty
e: Liquid volume tells how much liquid fits in a container.

q: What does it mean when a person earns income from working?
o: They pay someone else to work for them.
They receive money in exchange for their work.
They borrow money from a bank.
They put money into a savings account.
e: Income is the money people earn for doing work (labor).

q: A baker learns how to make wedding cakes and can now charge more for her work. Why can she earn more?
o: She borrowed money from a lender.
Her new skills and knowledge make her work more valuable.
e: Skills and knowledge (human capital) can raise the income a person earns.

q: Which is an example of labor?
o: A person painting houses for pay
e: Labor is the work people do. The other choices are tools and materials.

q: A storm destroys many orange trees, so there are fewer oranges to sell. What usually happens to the price of oranges?
o: The price stays the same no matter what.
e: When a resource is scarce, its price usually rises.

q: What does it mean when a resource is scarce?
o: There is not enough of it for everyone who wants it.
There is more than enough for everyone.
e: Scarcity means limited supply compared with what people want.

q: Only a few copies of a popular toy are left in the store, and many people want one. Why might the store raise the price?
o: Because the store wants to give it away.
Because the toy is scarce and many people want it.
e: Scarce goods that many people want tend to cost more.

q: Eli planned to save $20 for a book. At the store he buys a $15 toy he did not plan to buy. What is a cost of this unplanned spending?
o: He got the book for free.
He no longer has enough saved for the book.
e: Spending money on one thing means less money for something else.

q: Which is a benefit of planned spending?
o: You can make sure you have enough money for what you need.
You buy things as soon as you see them.
You never have to make choices.
e: A spending plan helps you set aside money for needs and goals.

q: Jo sees a toy on sale and buys it without thinking, even though her plan was to save for a bike. What kind of spending is this?
e: Spending that was not part of the plan is unplanned spending.

q: Sam borrows $30 from a lender and agrees to pay it back later with extra money added. What is the extra money called?
e: Interest is the fee a borrower pays for using a lender's money.

q: Who is responsible for paying back borrowed money?
o: the person who sells the item
e: The borrower must repay the lender, usually with interest.

q: When might a person use credit?
o: When what they want or need costs more than the money they have right now
When they are putting money away for later
When they never want to pay for anything
When they have much more money than they need
e: Credit lets people buy now and pay later, but they must pay it back.

q: Which is a good reason to save money?
o: To make sure you cannot buy what you need
To have money for something important later, like college
To spend it all right away
To make sure you owe more money later
e: Saving sets money aside for future needs and goals.

q: Ruby saves $5 every week. How much will she have saved after 4 weeks?
What is a savings plan?
o: A plan to spend all your money on wants
A list of things you owe
A plan to set aside part of your money regularly for a goal
e: A savings plan sets a goal and a regular amount to put away.

q: Which choice is an example of charitable giving?
o: Donating part of your allowance to a food bank
Putting money in your piggy bank
e: Charitable giving means giving money or goods to help others.

q: Dani gets $10 allowance. She puts $4 in savings, spends $5 on a toy, and gives $1 to an animal shelter. How much does she save?
e: The $4 put away is savings; $5 is spending and $1 is giving.

q: Lena earns $12 for walking dogs. She spends $7 on a book and puts the rest in a jar for a new bike. Which decision is saving?
o: Putting $5 in the jar for a bike
e: Saving means setting money aside for later: 12 − 7 = 5.
